title: Grateful Dead Live at Eureka Municipal Auditorium on 1968-01-20

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of a pre‑1970 treasure featuring first Clementine, New Potato, Born Cross‑Eyed and a stellar Spanish Jam, with crystal‑clear audio.
ai_review.review: The recording is praised as an “audio feast” – a pristine soundboard source where every instrument shines.  The show itself is highlighted for its rare early‑era material (the first Clementine, New Potato, Born Cross‑Eyed and the inaugural Spanish Jam) and remarkably smooth transitions that make it one of the band’s very best performances from this period.

ai_rating.rationale: All but one review are five‑star, extolling both the musical rarity and the excellent soundboard quality; the lone negative comment concerns missing track info only.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, clear mix with every instrument audible; no dropout or balance issues reported.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Rare early‑Dead material flows seamlessly with effortless transitions, giving the concert a cohesive, almost suite‑like feel.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Delivers spacious guitar work on New Potato and contributes strongly throughout.
band_member_comments.Phil: Wrote Clementine; his Coltrane influences are noted and his bass playing is praised as part of the overall feast.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen on keyboards is described as being at his best, adding depth to the jams.
